# AMD Instinct hardware validation campaign for vLLM ROCm serving

## Description

This epic resolves the hardware-dependent unknown at the core of the strategy:
whether vLLM serving on AMD Instinct accelerators reaches functional and
performance parity with the productized CUDA builds for the supported model
set. It delivers the validation campaign required by HLR-1 — including
securing access to physical AMD Instinct hardware, which does not exist in the
CI fleet today — and produces the go/no-go decision and cleared-model list
that define the scope of the serving runtime productization work.

## Scope

- Secure dedicated access to AMD Instinct nodes, via procurement or a partner
  lab (resolves the strategy's hardware-access open question), since no AMD
  GPU hardware exists in the CI fleet today
- Define the campaign protocol: the supported model set under test, functional
  pass/fail criteria per model, and performance parity benchmarks and
  go/no-go thresholds (against the CUDA runtime baseline) agreed before
  measurement
- Run functional validation of vLLM ROCm serving for each model in the
  supported model set on physical AMD Instinct hardware
- Run performance parity measurement (throughput and latency) per model
  against the CUDA baseline
- Produce the campaign report: per-model functional and performance results,
  the go/no-go recommendation, and the list of cleared models that bounds the
  productization scope
- Record the upstream vLLM ROCm image versions exercised by the campaign

## Acceptance Criteria

- A hardware access path (procurement or partner lab) is secured and
  documented, enabling hands-on validation on dedicated AMD Instinct nodes
- Given access to AMD Instinct nodes, when vLLM ROCm serving is exercised for
  each model in the supported model set, then a functional pass/fail result is
  recorded per model
- Performance parity metrics (throughput and latency) are captured per model
  against the CUDA baseline, with go/no-go thresholds defined before
  measurement
- The campaign report states a go/no-go recommendation and the cleared-model
  list that bounds the scope of the serving runtime productization

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): this epic is the validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct
  hardware that establishes functional and performance parity data and the
  go/no-go scope for productization
- Resolves the strategy's hardware-access open question and provides the
  scope-defining outcome for the HLR-2 productization work

# Upstream ROCm image cadence and alignment assessment

## Description

This epic resolves the strategy's open question on upstream ROCm build
cadence: whether upstream ROCm runtime image releases — controlled by AMD and
the upstream communities — align with the platform's release trains. Its
outcome determines the image sourcing strategy for the vLLM ROCm serving
runtime (consume-and-pin upstream images versus building and maintaining
images from source), and therefore what the productization work must do.

## Scope

- Inventory the upstream ROCm runtime image release history and published
  roadmap from AMD and the upstream communities (ROCm base images and the
  platform-relevant ROCm builds, vLLM serving foremost)
- Map each relevant upstream release against the platform release trains it
  could align with, covering recent history and the forward-looking horizon
- Identify misalignment risks (trains with no aligning upstream image) and
  their expected duration
- Produce a recommended image sourcing strategy (consume-and-pin upstream
  images vs build/maintain from source) with rationale, stating how the
  serving runtime productization approach changes under each cadence outcome

## Acceptance Criteria

- The assessment maps recent upstream ROCm runtime image releases to the
  platform release trains they could align with
- Known or expected misalignment gaps are identified with their timeframes
- A recommended image sourcing strategy is documented with rationale, stating
  what changes in the serving runtime productization approach under each
  cadence outcome

## HLR Traceability

- No direct HLR; resolves the strategy's upstream ROCm build cadence open
  question and gates the image sourcing approach of the HLR-2 serving runtime
  productization

# Productize supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime

## Description

This epic delivers HLR-2: a supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime, productized
for exactly the models the AMD Instinct validation campaign clears. It
packages the runtime for use under KServe InferenceServices and follows the
image sourcing strategy recommended by the upstream ROCm cadence assessment.

## Scope

- Package the vLLM ROCm serving runtime for the platform (runtime template
  and image), scoped to the models cleared by the validation campaign
- Follow the image sourcing strategy recommended by the upstream ROCm cadence
  assessment (consume-and-pin upstream images, or build/maintain from
  source), pinning the validated image version
- Validate the runtime under KServe InferenceServices on AMD Instinct nodes —
  KServe itself requires no code changes for this (it consumes runtimes
  through the runtime CRD); its compatibility is verified here
- Record the support statement inputs for the cleared model set on AMD
  Instinct hardware: supported hardware, driver prerequisites, and the
  validated model list

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the campaign-cleared model list, a vLLM ROCm serving runtime is
  productized and deployable for exactly those models (scope bounded by the
  campaign outcome)
- Given an InferenceService using the vLLM ROCm runtime on AMD Instinct
  nodes, inference requests complete successfully (functional validation
  under KServe)
- The runtime image version is pinned per the cadence assessment's
  recommended sourcing strategy, and the pin is documented
- The supported hardware, driver prerequisites, and cleared model list for
  the runtime are recorded for the platform support statement

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): a supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime is productized for the
  models the validation campaign clears
- The HLR-1 campaign outcome defines this epic's scope; the upstream cadence
  assessment outcome defines its image sourcing strategy

# Kueue amd.com/gpu quota handling for ROCm training

## Description

This epic delivers the Distributed Workloads (Kueue) share of HLR-3: ROCm
training jobs admitted through Kueue with amd.com/gpu quota handling,
including all-or-nothing (gang) admission for multi-GPU PyTorchJobs.

## Scope

- Define and validate ClusterQueue/LocalQueue quota configuration for the
  amd.com/gpu resource on AMD Instinct node pools
- Validate admission of PyTorchJobs requesting amd.com/gpu through Kueue
  queues: within-quota jobs admitted, over-quota jobs queued
- Validate all-or-nothing (gang) admission for multi-GPU PyTorchJobs
  requesting amd.com/gpu, together with the PyTorchJob-on-ROCm flow
- Document the quota configuration for AMD GPU resource flavors

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a queue configured with amd.com/gpu quota, a PyTorchJob requesting
  amd.com/gpu within quota is admitted, and one exceeding quota remains
  queued
- Given a multi-GPU PyTorchJob on ROCm, admission is all-or-nothing: the job
  runs only when all requested GPUs can be satisfied
- The amd.com/gpu quota configuration is documented for platform
  administrators

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): jobs admitted through Kueue, with amd.com/gpu quota handling
  (Distributed Workloads scope; PyTorchJob execution on ROCm is covered
  separately)
